_note: Coach-side content. Testimonials carry an ISO `datePublished` so they can be emitted as schema.org Review objects backing the AggregateRating on /coach.
_faqsNote: `faqs` is the single source for BOTH the /coach/faq accordion and the FAQPage JSON-LD on that route (faqPageSchema in lib/schema.ts), so a question added here appears in the page and in the rich result together and can never disagree with itself. Answers are plain text in Juliana's first-person voice — no HTML, no markdown, since the same string is rendered as JSX text and as schema.org `acceptedAnswer.text`. THE MONEY ANSWERS: the assessment answer must keep saying that a card is taken and nothing is charged (being coy about it converts worse and generates support email), and the billing answer must say '4 lessons a month' rather than 'every week' — 12 monthly bills cover 48 lessons while a year of true weekly lessons is ~52, so 'every week' is a promise the schedule cannot keep. See LESSONS_PER_MONTH in lib/pricing.ts. Nothing here may name a lesson address: in-person lessons happen in a private residence and the address goes out privately after booking (see content/pricing.json `_inPersonNote`). One hardcoded coupling to watch: the in-person answer names Tuesdays and Thursdays, which is IN_PERSON_DAYS in lib/pricing.ts — JSON cannot interpolate, so if that constant changes this answer has to change with it.
_voiceNote: VOICE RULES, applied across this file and the pages that read it. Contractions where they sound spoken — the copy audit measured 3.04:1 uncontracted-to-contracted site-wide, and uncontracted forms are what make a sentence read as carved rather than said. No triadic lists as the default cadence, no em-dash as the default connector, no closing sentence that restates the opening, no adjective stack without a concrete noun. Banned outright: elevate, unlock, delve, seamless, robust, utilize, 'in today's fast-paced world', 'it's not just X, it's Y', 'whether you're A or B'. Jargon carries a one-clause gloss the first time a non-musician meets it — 'ear training' and 'object writing' are glossed in the service bullets here, 'calibrated' is spelled out in the online-lessons answer rather than used as a word. Unfalsifiable claims are replaced with facts that exist in this repo: the Amanda Miguel tour, the Spotify editorial placements, the Hotel Café set, ages 5 to 70+, English/Spanish, five named five-star reviews. Nothing else may be asserted about students or outcomes.
_pendingFromOperator: NOT WRITEABLE FROM THIS REPO — do not let anyone infer these. (1) YEARS TEACHING. '7 years teaching' has been proposed in copy discussions and appears nowhere in this repo; no page may render a years-teaching figure until the true number is added here as a field. (2) STUDENT OUTCOMES. Zero outcomes exist anywhere on this site — the five testimonials describe warmth and patience, none describes anything that changed. A named, consented outcome ('sang at her sister's wedding after five months') is the single highest-value copy asset still missing. (3) TESTIMONIAL ENRICHMENT: for each of the five reviews, the discipline studied, months studied, online or in person, and parent-of-student or adult learner. (4) A SAFEGUARDING LINE the under-18 answer can point at (background check, parent policy). Until these arrive the copy stays with what is provably true.

faqs.q: Do I need experience to start?
faqs.a: No. Many of my students arrive having never sung outside their kitchen, and we start exactly where you are. There's no audition and nothing to prepare.
Kids, teens and adults. My students have ranged from age 5 to 70+, and I don't teach the ends of that range the same way.

Yes, both. For online lessons I don't leave the audio on default video-call settings: those are tuned for speech, so they gate your quiet notes and flatten anything soft. I set my end up for music and walk you through three settings on yours, once, at the start. All you need is wired headphones.
Pop, Latin Pop, Indie Pop, Singer-Songwriter, Acoustic, and contemporary styles. If you sing it from your real life, we can work on it.

faqs.q: Can you help me write original music?
faqs.a: Yes. Songwriting isn't a sideline here — I write and release my own records. We can start from a first lyric idea and carry on to a finished, released song, or stop wherever you want to stop.

faqs.q: Do I need to perform to take lessons?
faqs.a: No. Plenty of my students have no plans to sing in front of anyone, and that's a perfectly good reason to take lessons.

faqs.q: How often should I take lessons?
faqs.a: A weekly cadence is what actually changes a voice, which is why the monthly plans are built as 4 lessons a month. Every other week still works — it just takes longer to get to the same place, and you'll spend more of each lesson remembering where we were.

faqs.q: Do you help artists release music?
faqs.a: Yes. Artist development sessions can cover creative direction, performance coaching, branding and a release plan — whichever of those you actually need next.

faqs.q: What happens in the free 30-minute assessment?
faqs.a: We meet for thirty minutes, online or in person, and I listen to you sing. I map where your range sits today, what your voice is doing under pressure, and what you actually want to be able to do — then I tell you honestly how I'd get you there. You leave with something to work on whether or not you book anything else. It's free, and there's no audition to pass to get one.

faqs.q: Why do you ask for a card if the assessment is free?
faqs.a: To hold the slot, and only for that. Nothing is charged for the assessment — you'll see a $0 hold and no payment. The reason it exists is unglamorous: an assessment is a real hour out of my teaching week, and slots held with nothing behind them get forgotten. Keeping the card on file also means that if you do decide to carry on, starting lessons is one click instead of another checkout.

A monthly plan covers 4 lessons a month at a weekly cadence, billed once a month on the same date. I say four a month rather than 'every week' on purpose: some months have five of your weekday, and I'd rather the number in your plan be the number you can hold me to. If a fifth lesson suits us both, we can add it as a single lesson.

faqs.q: When is my first payment taken?
faqs.a: A week after your assessment, so the first bill lands after you've had your first proper lesson and know whether this is for you. Nothing is taken at the assessment itself.

faqs.q: Can I cancel, or take a break?
faqs.a: Cancel any time — there's no notice period and no contract to see out. You keep the lessons you've already paid for. And if life gets in the way rather than ends the lessons, you can pause your plan for one month, once a year, at no cost: no billing, your slot held. Just tell me before the next billing date so I'm not charging you for a month you're away.

In person in Los Angeles, on Tuesdays and Thursdays. I teach from a private space rather than a commercial studio, so I share the exact address with you privately once your lesson is confirmed. If those two days don't work, online is the same lesson — several of my longest-running students have never been in the room.

faqs.q: Can you teach a student under 18?
faqs.a: Yes, and I love teaching younger students — mine have started as young as five. A parent or guardian books the lessons, and it's the guardian's card that goes on file and their name on the account. You're welcome to sit in, especially for the first few lessons with a younger child; some students settle faster with a parent in the room and some without, and we'll work out which yours is.

Every price is on the pricing page. Nothing here is quote-on-request. Prices are for the lesson slot rather than the subject, so a 60-minute lesson costs the same whether we spend it on voice, guitar, piano or songwriting. Monthly plans work out cheaper per lesson than single lessons, because consistent weeks are what actually make a voice change.
